grammar.explanation_en: Possessive adjectives show who something belongs to. They always come before a noun: 'my mother', 'his brother', 'her friend'. They never change form, no matter the noun's number.
grammar.explanation_ko: 소유 형용사는 무언가가 누구의 것인지 나타내며, 항상 명사 앞에 옵니다: 'my mother'(내 어머니), 'his brother'(그의 형), 'her friend'(그녀의 친구). 명사가 단수든 복수든 형태가 바뀌지 않습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: Is this a picture of your family?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: Yes! This is my mother, and this is my brother.
dialogue.line_ko: 네! 이분은 제 어머니이고, 이 사람은 제 형이에요.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: Yes, he is. He's also very kind.

reading.title: My Family
reading.text: I have a small family. My father is a teacher, and my mother is a doctor. I have one sister. She is younger than me. She is kind and friendly. My grandmother lives with us too. She is 75 years old.
reading.text_ko: 저희 가족은 단출해요. 아버지는 선생님이시고, 어머니는 의사세요. 저는 여동생이 한 명 있어요. 저보다 어려요. 여동생은 친절하고 다정해요. 할머니도 저희와 함께 사세요. 할머니는 75세이세요.

explanation.en: The text says 'My father is a teacher.'
explanation.ko: 본문에 'My father is a teacher.'라고 나옵니다.

explanation.en: The text says 'She is kind and friendly.'
explanation.ko: 본문에 'She is kind and friendly.'라고 나옵니다.

explanation.en: The text says 'She is 75 years old.'
